sections.html: Hara jerdoni is a tiny moth catfish that attains only a length of 2-3 cm and has very, very long pectoral fin spines. In some swimming positions it looks like a passenger airplane.

Moth cats (Hara) occur in India, Burma, and Thailand. The species are very difficult to tell apart, in many cases it is simply impossible in live animals. There are a few species that can be determined by a filament on the caudal fin, but most of the species are extremely similar looking. Hara jerdoni is an exception to this rule.
Since Hara in general do not swim a lot, all species can be kept in small tanks.
Moth catfish are very peaceful towards conspecifics and other fish.
